blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines —Sen. Mark Villar called for stronger and more coordinated measures to safeguard the country’s food security amid the looming threat of Super El Niño, warning that prolonged dry conditions could disrupt food production and distribution, drive up prices, and put vulnerable Filipino households at risk. In a statement, Villar cited a report from the Office of Civil Defense putting agricultural damage caused by El Niño at ₱6.8 billion as of October 2026, with 109 areas declaring a state of calamity.
